Novozlatopil Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zaporizhia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Novozlatopil was founded in 1848 as Jewish Colony Number 1 by settlers from the Mogilev, Vitebsk, and Kovno Governorates. During the Civil War of 1918–21, well-organized Jewish self-defense successfully prevented pogroms here — a rare, effective outcome in this collection. In the 1920s, the colony became the center of its own Novozlatopil Jewish National Raion, one of at least four such Jewish administrative districts documented in this collection; its secular Yiddish culture included two schools, an animal-husbandry college, a library, and its own newspaper, Der Kolvirt Shtern ('The Kolkhoz Star'). About two-thirds of the colony's Jews evacuated before the Germans arrived in October 1941, and about 700 from Novozlatopil and nearby communities were murdered in February 1942; of the roughly 250 who returned after the war, most soon relocated to large cities or to Birobidzhan, the Soviet Union's official Jewish autonomous region in the Far East.
